name: Songhai Empire

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 600,000-700,000 km2 for the Askiya dynasty (1493-1591); the world_1500 polygon measures ~609,000 km2. Later expansion (infobox 1.4 million km2 in 1528) is after this snapshot.

population.note: Seshat codes 4-5 million for 1493-1591 (suspected). Low: OWID/HYDE Mali + Niger 1500 = 1.9 million in modern borders (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) plus the Inland Delta share; 1500 is early in the Askiya expansion.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Gao ~60,000 in 1512 (Seshat largest settlement), Timbuktu and Djenne.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Askia Muhammad replaced the general levy with a professional army of slave soldiers (Levtzion 1977 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Askia_Muhammad_I); no count survives for 1500. At Tondibi (1591) the Songhai fielded 12,500-18,000 cavalry and 9,700-30,000 infantry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tondibi), a larger later state.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Provincial levies of the Kurmina, Dendi and central provinces, Sorko boatmen and Tuareg contingents.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Crews of the river fleet under the hi-koy (admiral).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Sahelian state with slave soldiers and tributary levies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Mailed lancers of the askiya's household and provincial governors.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: mail and quilted horse armour, lance and sword, no firearms.

count.note: Educated guess. Mounted archers and Tuareg camel and horse riders.
Educated guess. Archers with poisoned arrows.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: bows against an arquebus-era best.

count.note: Educated guess. Spear and sword infantry of the standing army.
The hi-koy at Gao commanded more than a thousand boats (the article); further flotillas at Kabara and Ayorou. Dugout war and transport canoes.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: Askia Muhammad built on Sonni Ali's conquests (Timbuktu 1468, Djenne 1473) with a professional army.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: slave soldiers bound to the askiya; Sonni-Askiya succession conflict recent (1493).

morale.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: expansion and jihad against the Mossi after the 1496-98 hajj.

weapons.note: Anchor 3-4: iron lances, swords, bows; no firearms until the Moroccan invasion of 1591.

armor.note: Anchor 3-4: mail for elite cavalry, quilted horse armour.

logistics.note: Anchor 3: Niger river transport and granaries.

gdpPerCapita.note: Educated guess. No Maddison estimate for West Africa before 1950; Egypt 1500 = 1,084 (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) is an upper reference. Subsistence farming lifted by gold, salt and trans-Saharan trade; same basis as mali-empire-1330.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Standing slave army fed from royal estates.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Inland Niger Delta rice and millet; royal slave estates.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. River ports: Gao, Kabara (Timbuktu), Djenne, Ayorou.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. River-borne supply along the Niger; seasonal limits in the rains.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, camels, oxen and donkeys.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: Sahara crossing and heat for northern invaders, river mobility; open terrain.

notes: Snapshot = 1500, Askia Muhammad I (r. 1493-1528) after his hajj, early in the Askiya expansion. Personnel convention: the askiya's professional slave army and fleet are activePersonnel; provincial and tributary levies are trainedReserves. No contemporary count exists for 1500: the Tarikh al-Sudan and Leo Africanus give impressions, and the Tondibi (1591) figures describe the later, larger state; force numbers are educated guesses (grade D). Hunwick (Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire) and Thornton not consulted directly. Population convention: Gao, the Niger bend, Timbuktu and the Inland Delta (Djenne); Hausa and Air tributaries of later years excluded.
